title: Adding machine
about: Type of mechanical calculator designed to perform basic arithmetic
blurb: An adding machine is a class of mechanical calculator, usually specialized for bookkeeping calculations. Consequently, the earliest adding machines were often designed to read in particular currencies.

title: Amazon Kindle
blurb: Amazon Kindle is a series of e-readers designed and marketed by Amazon. Amazon Kindle devices enable users to browse, buy, download, and read e-books, newspapers, magazines, Audible audiobooks, and other digital media via wireless networking to the Kindle Store.

title: Amiga
about: Family of personal computers sold by Commodore
blurb: Amiga is a family of personal computers produced by Commodore from 1985 until the company's bankruptcy in 1994, with production by others afterward. When introduced, it was one of a number of mid-1980s computers with 16-bit or 32-bit processors, 256 KB or more of RAM, and mouse-based GUIs.

title: Apple Vision Pro
blurb: The Apple Vision Pro is a head-worn computer developed by Apple. It was announced on June 5, 2023, at Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference and was released first in the US, then in global territories throughout 2024.

title: Apple Watch
blurb: The Apple Watch is a line of smartwatches developed and marketed by Apple. It has fitness tracking, health-oriented capabilities, and wireless telecommunication, integrating with watchOS and other Apple products and services.

title: Atari 2600
blurb: The Atari 2600 is a home video game console developed and produced by Atari, Inc. Released c. September 1977 as the Atari Video Computer System, it popularized microprocessor-based hardware and games stored on swappable ROM cartridges, a format first used with the Fairchild Channel F in 1976.

title: Atari 5200
blurb: The Atari 5200 is a home video game console introduced in 1982 by Atari, Inc. as a higher-end complement for the popular Atari Video Computer System. The VCS was renamed to Atari 2600 at the time of the 5200's launch.

title: Atari 7800
blurb: The Atari 7800 ProSystem, or simply the Atari 7800, is a home video game console released by Atari Corporation in May 1986 as the successor to both the Atari 2600 and Atari 5200. It can run almost all Atari 2600 cartridges, making it the first console with backward compatibility.

title: Atari Jaguar
blurb: The Atari Jaguar is a home video game console developed by Atari Corporation and released in North America in November 1993. Atari marketed it as the world's first 64-bit game system, drawing controversy as some argued that this configuration did not meet the definition of a 64-bit system.

title: Canon EOS 2000D
blurb: The Canon EOS 2000D, known as the Rebel T7 in the Americas, as the Kiss X90 in Japan and as the 1500D in southeast Asia, is a 24.1 megapixels digital single-lens reflex camera made by Canon.

title: Canon EOS 5D
blurb: The Canon EOS 5D is a 12.7 megapixel full-frame digital single-lens reflex camera body produced by Canon.

title: Canon EOS 5D Mark II
blurb: The Canon EOS 5D Mark II is a 21.0 effective megapixel full-frame CMOS digital single-lens reflex camera made by Canon, the first Canon EOS camera to have video recording capabilities. It succeeds the EOS 5D and was announced on 17 September 2008.

title: Canon EOS 5D Mark IV
blurb: The Canon EOS 5D Mark IV is a professional-grade 30.4-megapixel full-frame digital single-lens reflex camera made by Canon.

title: Canon PowerShot G
blurb: The Canon PowerShot G is a series of digital cameras introduced by Canon in its PowerShot line in 2000.

title: Casio ClassPad 300
about: Family of graphing calculators by Casio
blurb: The Casio ClassPad 300, ClassPad 330 and fx-CP400 are stylus based touch-screen graphing calculators. It comes with a collection of applications that support self-study, like 3D Graph, Geometry, eActivity, Spreadsheet, etc. A large 160x240 pixel LCD touch screen enables stylus-based operation.

title: Casio fx-7000G
blurb: The Casio FX-7000G is a calculator which is widely known as being the world's first graphing calculator available to the public. It was introduced to the public and later manufactured between 1985 and c. 1989. Notable features are its ability to graph functions, and that it is programmable.

title: Casio graphic calculators
about: Overview of the graphic calculators made by Casio
blurb: Casio produced the world's first graphing calculator, the fx-7000G. Since then, the company has released many more graphic calculators, with the FX-CG100 being the newest.

title: ColecoVision
blurb: The ColecoVision is a second-generation home video game console developed by Coleco and launched in North America in August 1982. It was released later in July 1983 in Europe by CBS Electronics as the CBS ColecoVision.

title: Curta
blurb: The Curta is a hand-held mechanical calculator designed by Curt Herzstark. It is known for its extremely compact design: a small cylinder that fits in the palm of the hand.

title: Dreamcast
blurb: The Dreamcast is the final home video game console manufactured by Sega. It was released in Japan on November 27, 1998, and worldwide in late 1999. It succeeded the Sega Saturn and was the first sixth-generation console, preceding Sony's PlayStation 2, Nintendo's GameCube, and Microsoft's Xbox.

title: DynaTAC
blurb: The DynaTAC is a series of cellular telephones manufactured by Motorola from 1983 to 1994. Unveiled on March 6, 1983, the DynaTAC was the first commercially available handheld cellular phone. A full charge took roughly 10 hours, and it offered 30 minutes of talk time.

title: Fairchild Channel F
about: First ROM cartridge–based video game console
blurb: The Fairchild Channel F, short for "Channel Fun", is a home video game console, the first to be based on a microprocessor and to use ROM cartridges instead of having games built in.

title: Fuji GX680
blurb: The Fuji GX680 is a series of single lens reflex system cameras for medium format film produced by Fujifilm with interchangeable camera lenses and interchangeable film holders for the unusual film format 6×8 cm on 120 and 220 roll film.

title: Fujifilm X-T5
blurb: The Fujifilm X-T5 is a mirrorless interchangeable-lens digital camera announced on November 2, 2022. It is the successor to 2020's X-T4 with improved autofocus, higher resolution and reduced body size.

title: Fujifilm X100
blurb: The Fujifilm X100 is a series of digital compact cameras with a fixed prime lens. Originally part of the FinePix line, then becoming a member of the X series from Fujifilm, the X100 series includes the FinePix X100, X100S, X100T, X100F, X100V, and X100VI.

title: Game Boy
blurb: Nintendo's grey 1989 handheld with a green-tinted screen and a copy of Tetris in the box.

title: Game Boy Advance
blurb: The Game Boy Advance is a handheld game console developed and marketed by Nintendo, which was released in Japan on March 21, 2001, and in other regions in June. It was later released in mainland China in 2004, under the name iQue Game Boy Advance.

title: GameCube
blurb: The GameCube, officially known as Nintendo GameCube, is a home video game console developed and marketed by Nintendo. It was released in Japan on September 14, 2001, in North America on November 18, 2001, and in Europe on May 3, 2002.

title: Google Pixel
blurb: Google Pixel is a brand of portable consumer electronic devices developed by Google that runs the Pixel version of the Android operating system or the ChromeOS operating system.

title: Gyrocompass
about: Type of non-magnetic compass based on the rotation of the Earth
blurb: A gyrocompass or Gyrocompassing is a type of non-magnetic compass which is based on a fast-spinning disc and the rotation of the Earth to find geographical direction automatically. A gyrocompass makes use of one of the seven fundamental ways to determine the heading of a vehicle.

title: Handycam
about: Brand name used by Sony for its camcorder lineup
blurb: Handycam is a line of camcorders made by Sony and introduced in 1985. Handycam was first used as the name of the first Video8 camcorder in 1985, replacing Sony's previous line of Betamax-based models of camcorders.

title: Holga
blurb: The Holga is a medium format 120 film camera, made in Hong Kong, known for its low-fidelity aesthetic. The Holga's low-cost construction and simple meniscus lens often yields pictures that display vignetting, blur, light leaks and other distortions.

title: HP 48 series
blurb: The HP 48 is a series of graphing calculators designed and produced by Hewlett-Packard from 1990 until 2003. The series includes the HP 48S, HP 48SX, HP 48G, HP 48GX, and HP 48G+, the G models being expanded and improved versions of the S models.

title: HP 49/50 series
about: Series of graphing calculators by Hewlett-Packard
blurb: The HP 49/50 series are Hewlett-Packard manufactured graphing calculators. They are the successors of the HP 48 series. There are five calculators in the 49/50 series of HP graphing calculators.

title: HP Prime
blurb: The HP Prime Graphing Calculator is a graphing calculator introduced by Hewlett-Packard in 2013 and manufactured by HP Inc. until the licensees Moravia Consulting spol. s r.o.

title: HP-12C
blurb: The HP-12C is a financial calculator made by Hewlett-Packard and its successor HP Inc. as part of the HP Voyager series, introduced in 1981. It is HP's longest running and best-selling product and is considered the de facto standard among financial professionals.

title: HP-35
blurb: The HP-35 was Hewlett-Packard's first pocket calculator and the world's first scientific pocket calculator: a calculator with trigonometric and exponential functions. It was introduced in 1972.

title: HTC Dream
blurb: The HTC Dream is a smartphone developed by HTC. First released in October 2008 for US$179 with a 2-year contract to T-Mobile, the Dream was the first commercially released device to use the Linux-based Android operating system, which was purchased and further developed by Google and the Open…

title: HTC Vive
blurb: HTC Vive is a line of virtual and mixed reality headsets produced by HTC Corporation. The brand currently encompasses headsets designed for use with personal computers as well as standalone headsets such as the Vive Focus line, Vive Flow glasses, and the Vive Elite XR headset.

title: Instax
about: Brand of instant cameras by Fujifilm
blurb: Instax is a brand of instant still cameras and instant films marketed by Fujifilm. The first camera and accompanying film, the Instax Mini 10 and Instax Mini film, were released on November 10, 1998. The "Wide" film and first accompanying camera were released the following year.

title: iPad
about: Line of tablet computers by Apple
blurb: The iPad is a brand of tablet computers developed and marketed by Apple since 2010. The first-generation iPad was introduced on January 27, 2010. Since then, the iPad product line has been expanded to include the smaller iPad Mini, the lighter and thinner iPad Air, and the flagship iPad Pro models.

title: iPad Mini
blurb: The iPad Mini is a line of small tablet computers developed and marketed by Apple. It is a sub-series of the iPad line of tablets, with screen sizes of 7.9 inches to 8.5 inches.

title: iPad Mini (A20 Pro)
blurb: The eighth-generation iPad Mini) is a tablet computer in the iPad Mini line, developed and marketed by Apple. It was announced on October 26, 2026, and it was released on November 6, 2026. Its predecessor, the seventh-generation iPad Mini, was discontinued on the same day.

title: iPad Pro
blurb: The iPad Pro is a series of tablet computers, positioned as the premium line of Apple's iPad brand. Models run iPadOS, a tablet-optimized fork of the iOS operating system. Early models were distinguished from other iPads by their ability to use the Apple Pencil stylus and their larger screen size.

title: iPhone
blurb: The iPhone is a smartphone developed and marketed by Apple as the first device in the iPhone lineup of smartphones. It features a Samsung S5L8900 SoC, a 3.5 in multi-touch display, and a web browser.

title: iPhone 13
blurb: The iPhone 13 and iPhone 13 Mini are smartphones that were developed and marketed by Apple. They are the fifteenth generation of iPhones, succeeding the iPhone 12 and 12 Mini.

title: iPhone 17 Pro
blurb: The iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max are smartphones developed and marketed by Apple. Alongside the iPhone 17 and iPhone Air, they form the nineteenth generation of the iPhone, succeeding the iPhone 16 Pro and iPhone 16 Pro Max.

title: iPhone 18 Pro
blurb: The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are smartphones developed and marketed by Apple. Alongside the iPhone Duo, they form the twentieth generation of the iPhone, succeeding the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max.

title: iPhone Duo
blurb: The iPhone Duo is the first foldable smartphone by Apple. The device was announced during an Apple event at Apple Park in Cupertino, California, on September 9, 2026, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, and was released on October 23, 2026.

title: iPod
blurb: Apple's 2001 music player with a click wheel: a thousand songs in your pocket.

title: iPod Mini
about: Digital audio player by Apple Computer
blurb: The iPod Mini is a digital audio player that was designed and marketed by Apple Computer. It was positioned as a smaller, midrange model in Apple's iPod product line to complement the iPod Classic. The device was announced on January 6, 2004, and released on February 20 of the same year.

title: iPod Nano
about: Discontinued line of portable media players by Apple
blurb: The iPod Nano is a discontinued portable media player designed and formerly marketed by Apple. The first-generation model was introduced on September 7, 2005, as a replacement for the iPod Mini, using flash memory for storage.

title: iPod Touch
about: Mobile device made by Apple Inc.
blurb: The seventh generation iPod Touch or iPod touch 7) is a discontinued mobile device designed and marketed by Apple Inc. with a touchscreen-based user interface. It is the successor to the 6th-generation iPod Touch, the first major update to the line since 2015.

title: iPod Touch (4th generation)
about: Mobile device made by Apple Inc.
blurb: The iPod Touch 4th generation is a multi-touch mobile device designed and marketed by Apple Inc. with a touchscreen-based user interface. The successor to the 3rd-generation iPod Touch, it was unveiled at Apple's media event on September 1, 2010, and was released on September 12, 2010.

title: iPod Touch (5th generation)
about: Mobile device made by Apple Inc.
blurb: The fifth generation iPod Touch is a mobile device designed and marketed by Apple Inc. with a touchscreen-based user interface. The successor to the 4th-generation iPod Touch, it was unveiled at Apple's media event alongside the iPhone 5 on September 12, 2012, and was released on October 11, 2012.

title: Jukebox
blurb: A coin-operated machine full of records, glowing in the corner of a diner.

title: Kodak Brownie
blurb: The Brownie was a series of camera models made by Eastman Kodak and first released in 1900. It introduced the snapshot to the masses by addressing the cost factor that had kept amateur photography beyond many people's means; the Pocket Kodak, for example, cost most families in Britain nearly a…

title: Leica M3
blurb: The Leica M3 is a 35 mm rangefinder camera by Ernst Leitz GmbH, introduced in 1954. It was a new starting point for Leitz, which until then had only produced screw-mount Leica cameras that were incremental improvements to its original Leica.

title: Leica M6
blurb: The Leica M6 is a 35mm rangefinder film camera manufactured by Leica from 1984 to 1998, followed by the M6 "TTL" manufactured from 1998 to 2002. In 2022, Leica introduced a new version of the M6, based on the technology of the Leica MP, but staying true to the design of the M6.

title: Mamiya 645
about: Series of film and digital cameras and lenses
blurb: The Mamiya 645 camera systems are a series of medium format film and digital cameras and lenses manufactured by Mamiya and its successors. They are called "645" because they use the nominal 6 cm x 4.5 cm film size from 120 roll film.

title: Mamiya RZ67
blurb: The Mamiya RZ67 is a professional medium format single-lens reflex camera manufactured by Mamiya. There are three successive models: the RZ67 Professional, RZ67 Professional II and RZ67 Professional IID. It is primarily designed for studio use, but can also be used in the field.

title: Microsoft Surface
about: Series of personal computers, tablets and interactive whiteboards by Microsoft
blurb: Microsoft Surface is a family of touchscreen-based personal computer, tablet, and interactive whiteboard hardware products designed and developed by Microsoft.

title: Motorola Razr V3
blurb: The Motorola Razr V3, popularly called simply the Razr, is a flip phone developed by Motorola. A 2G quad-band worldwide GSM phone, it was released initially in September 2004, and in the US in November 2004, being the first product released under the RAZR moniker.

title: Nex Playground
blurb: The Nex Playground is a video game console developed by Nex that was released in December 2023. It uses motion capture to encourage indoor active play.

title: Nikkormat
blurb: Nikkormat was a brand of cameras produced by the Japanese optics company Nippon Kogaku K. K., as a consumer version of the professional Nikon brand.

title: Nikon D750
blurb: The Nikon D750 is a full-frame DSLR camera announced by Nikon on September 12, 2014. It is an extensive upgrade from the D610, but with the same general body and control characteristics, along with 24 megapixel resolution.

title: Nikon F
blurb: The Nikon F camera, introduced in April 1959, was Nikon's first SLR camera. It was one of the most advanced cameras of its day. Although many of the concepts had already been introduced elsewhere, it was revolutionary in that it was the first to combine them all in one camera.

title: Nikon F2
blurb: The Nikon F2 is a professional-level 35 mm single-lens reflex camera. It was manufactured by the Japanese optics company Nippon Kogaku K. K. in Japan from September 1971 to 1980.

title: Nikon F3
blurb: The Nikon F3 is Nikon's third professional single-lens reflex camera body, preceded by the F and F2. Introduced in March 1980, it has manual and semi-automatic exposure control whereby the camera would select the correct shutter speed.

title: Nikon Z8
blurb: The Nikon Z8 is a high-end full-frame mirrorless camera produced by Nikon. The camera was announced on May 10, 2023. It is the tenth Z-mount camera body and the seventh full-frame Z-mount body.

title: Nintendo 3DS
blurb: The Nintendo 3DS is a foldable dual-screen handheld game console developed and marketed by Nintendo. Announced in March 2010 and released beginning in early 2011, it succeeds the Nintendo DS and DSi.

title: Nintendo 64
blurb: The Nintendo 64 is a home video game console developed and marketed by Nintendo. It was released in Japan on June 23, 1996, in North America on September 29, 1996, and in Europe and Australia on March 1, 1997.

title: Nintendo DS
blurb: The Nintendo DS is a foldable handheld game console developed by Nintendo and released worldwide between 2004 and 2005.

title: Nintendo Entertainment System
blurb: The Nintendo Entertainment System is a home video game console developed and marketed by Nintendo. It was released as the Family Computer in Japan on July 15, 1983, and as the NES in test markets in the United States on October 18, 1985, followed by a nationwide launch on September 27, 1986.

title: Nintendo Switch
blurb: The Nintendo Switch is a video game console developed by Nintendo and released worldwide in most regions on March 3, 2017.

title: Nokia 3210
blurb: The Nokia 3210 is a GSM cell phone, announced by Nokia at the CeBIT fair on March 18, 1999, alongside the Nokia 7110.

title: Nokia 3310
blurb: The Nokia 3310 is a discontinued GSM mobile phone by Nokia. It was announced on the 1st of September 2000, and released in the fourth quarter of the year, replacing the popular Nokia 3210.

title: Nokia 5110
blurb: The Nokia 5110 is a GSM mobile phone that was introduced by Nokia on 12 April 1998. The 5110 was intended for the consumer market, succeeding the Nokia 3110 and the analogue Nokia 232, and it based on the same platform as the business-oriented Nokia 6110, giving it additional features such as games…

title: Nokia N95
about: Mobile phone released by Nokia in 2007
blurb: The Nokia N95 and Nokia N95 8GB are high-end mobile phones produced by Nokia as part of their former Nseries line of multimedia mobile devices. Announced in September 2006, it was released to the market in March 2007. The N95 runs S60 3rd Edition, on Symbian OS v9.2.

title: Nothing Phone 1
blurb: The Nothing Phone, stylised as Phone is an Android smartphone by Nothing. The phone was announced on 23 March 2022 and went on sale on 21 July 2022.

title: Oculus Rift
about: Virtual reality headsets by Oculus VR
blurb: Oculus Rift is a discontinued line of virtual reality headsets developed and manufactured by Oculus VR, a virtual reality company founded by Palmer Luckey.

title: Olympus OM-1
blurb: The Olympus OM-1 is a manually operated 35mm single-lens reflex professional camera, part of the Olympus OM system. It was manufactured by Olympus Optical Co., Ltd., later Olympus Corporation, in Japan between 1972 and 1988.

title: OM System OM-1
blurb: The OM System OM-1 is the flagship mirrorless interchangeable-lens camera produced by OM Digital Solutions on the micro four-thirds system. It is the first high-end digital camera made by OM Digital Solutions after its acquisition of the imaging divisions of the camera manufacturer Olympus.

title: Optical telescope
about: Telescope for observations with visible light
blurb: An optical telescope gathers and focuses light mainly from the visible part of the electromagnetic spectrum, to create a magnified image for direct visual inspection, to make a photograph, or to collect data through electronic image sensors.

title: Pentax 6×7
blurb: The Pentax 6×7 is a SLR medium format system film camera for 120 and 220 film, which produces images on the film that are nominally 6 cm by 7 cm in size, made by Pentax. It originally debuted in 1965 as a prototype dubbed the Pentax 220.

title: Pentax K1000
blurb: The Pentax K1000 is an interchangeable lens, 35 mm film, single-lens reflex camera, manufactured by Asahi Optical Co., Ltd. from 1976 to 1997, originally in Japan. The Pentax K1000 eventually sold over three million units.

title: Pentax Spotmatic
about: Family of cameras by Asahi Optical Co. Ltd
blurb: The Pentax Spotmatic, originally marked the Asahi Pentax Spotmatic, refers to a family of 35mm single-lens reflex cameras manufactured by the Asahi Optical Co. Ltd., later known as Pentax Corporation, between 1964 and 1976.

title: Phonograph
blurb: A machine that plays sound from a groove in a spinning disc or cylinder, through a needle and a horn.

title: Pixel 10
blurb: The Pixel 10 is an Android smartphone designed, developed, and marketed by Google as part of the Google Pixel product line. It was announced on August 20, 2025 at the Made by Google keynote in Brooklyn, New York.

title: Pixel 10a
blurb: The Pixel 10a is an Android-based smartphone designed, developed, and marketed by Google as part of the Google Pixel product line. It serves as a mid-range variant of the Pixel 10 series, with similarities in design, software, and other features to its more premium counterparts.

title: Pixel 11
blurb: The Pixel 11 is an Android-based smartphone designed, developed, manufactured, and marketed by Google as part of the Google Pixel product line. It serves as the successor to the Pixel 10, with a similar feature set and design.

title: Playdate
about: A yellow pocket game console with a crank
blurb: It's yellow, it fits in your pocket and there's a crank. Playdate, from Panic in Portland, Oregon, comes with 24 free games.

title: PlayStation
about: Home video game console by Sony
blurb: The PlayStation is a home video game console developed and marketed by Sony Computer Entertainment. It was released in Japan on 3 December 1994, followed by North America on 9 September 1995, Europe on 29 September 1995, and other regions following thereafter.

title: PlayStation 2
about: Home video game console by Sony
blurb: The PlayStation 2 is a home video game console developed by Sony Computer Entertainment. It was first released in Japan on March 4, 2000, in North America on October 26, in Europe on November 24, in Australia on November 30, and other regions thereafter.

title: PlayStation 4
about: Home video game console by Sony
blurb: The PlayStation 4 is a home video game console developed by Sony Interactive Entertainment. Announced as the successor to the PlayStation 3 in February 2013, it was launched on November 15, 2013, in North America, November 29, 2013, in Europe, South America, and Australia, and on February 22, 2014,…

title: PlayStation Portable
blurb: The PlayStation Portable is a handheld game console developed and marketed by Sony Computer Entertainment. It was first released in Japan on December 12, 2004, in North America on March 24, 2005, and in PAL regions on September 1, 2005.

title: PlayStation Vita
blurb: The PlayStation Vita is a handheld game console developed and marketed by Sony Computer Entertainment. It was first released in Japan on December 17, 2011, then in other international territories on February 22, 2012, and was produced until discontinuation on March 1, 2019.

title: Polaroid SX-70
blurb: A folding instant camera of 1972 that ejects a photograph and lets you watch it develop.

title: Ranga Pens
about: Handmade fountain pens from near Chennai
blurb: A pen company started by Pandurangan in Thiruvallur, near Chennai, in 1970, making handmade fountain and roller pens.

title: Ricoh GR digital cameras
blurb: The Ricoh GR is a series of point-and-shoot, or compact, digital cameras made by Ricoh. The GR name was previously used for Ricoh's GR series of film cameras. Like the GR film cameras and Fujifilm X70, the GR digital cameras use metal bodies fitted with bright, permanently-attached prime lenses.

title: Samsung Galaxy
about: Series of Android smartphones, mobile computing device and Android applications
blurb: Samsung Galaxy is a series of mobile computing devices designed, manufactured, and marketed by Samsung Electronics since 2009.

title: Samsung Galaxy A series
about: Mid-range series of smartphones by Samsung Electronics
blurb: The Samsung Galaxy A series is a line of entry-level and mid-range Android-based smartphones and tablets manufactured and developed by Samsung Electronics as part of their Galaxy line, succeeding both the Galaxy J series and the Galaxy S "mini" line and slotted below the flagship Galaxy S series.

title: Sega Genesis
blurb: The Sega Genesis, known as the Mega Drive outside North America, is a 16-bit fourth generation home video game console developed and sold by Sega. It was Sega's third console and the successor to the Master System.

title: Sega Saturn
blurb: The Sega Saturn is a home video game console developed by Sega and released on November 22, 1994, in Japan, May 11, 1995, in North America, and July 8, 1995, in Europe. Part of the fifth generation of video game consoles, it is the successor to the successful Genesis.

title: Sinclair Executive
blurb: The Sinclair Executive was the world's first "slimline" pocket calculator, and the first to be produced by Clive Sinclair's company Sinclair Radionics.

title: Sinclair Scientific
blurb: The Sinclair Scientific was a 12-function, pocket-sized scientific calculator introduced in 1974, dramatically undercutting in price other calculators available at the time. The Sinclair Scientific Programmable, released a year later, was advertised as the first budget programmable calculator.

title: Sony α6000
blurb: The Sony α6000 is a digital camera announced 12 February 2014. It is a mirrorless interchangeable lens camera, which has a smaller body form factor than a traditional DSLR while retaining the sensor size and features of an APS-C-sized model.

title: Sony α7
blurb: The Sony α7, α7R, α7S and α7C are four closely related families of full-frame mirrorless interchangeable-lens cameras. The first two were announced in October 2013, the third in April 2014 and the fourth in September 2020.

title: Sony α7 IV
blurb: The Sony α7 IV is a full-frame mirrorless interchangeable-lens camera manufactured by Sony. It was announced on 21 October 2021 as the successor to the Sony α7 III.

title: Steam Frame
blurb: The Steam Frame is a virtual reality headset developed by Valve. It was announced in November 2025 as part of a broader Steam hardware lineup. It launched on September 14, 2026 with a sign up system, with randomized order emails going out 4 days later.

title: Super Nintendo Entertainment System
blurb: The Super Nintendo Entertainment System is a home video game console developed and marketed by Nintendo. It was released as the Super Famicom in Japan on November 21, 1990, as the Super NES in North America on August 23, 1991, and internationally throughout 1992.

title: Swiss Army knife
blurb: A red pocket knife that unfolds into blades, scissors, a corkscrew and, somewhere, a toothpick.

title: TI-84 Plus CE series
blurb: The TI-84 Plus CE series is a line of graphing calculators manufactured by Texas Instruments. The original TI-84 Plus CE superseded the TI-84 Plus series upon its introduction in 2015; together with the TI-Nspire series, the TI-84 Plus CE is the previous generation flagship series of Texas…

title: TI-84 Plus series
about: Line of graphing calculators produced by Texas Instruments
blurb: The TI-84 Plus series is a line of graphing calculators produced by Texas Instruments. They are ubiquitous in the American education system, and have historically been considered the de facto standard in grade school math.

title: TI-89 series
blurb: The TI-89 and the TI-89 Titanium are graphing calculators developed by Texas Instruments. They are differentiated from most other TI graphing calculators by their computer algebra system, which allows symbolic manipulation of algebraic expressions—equations can be solved in terms of variables—…

title: TI-Nspire series
blurb: The TI-Nspire is a graphing calculator line made by Texas Instruments, with the first version released on 25 September 2007.[better source needed] The calculators feature a non-QWERTY keyboard and a different key-by-key layout than Texas Instruments's previous flagship calculators such as the TI-89…

title: TurboGrafx-16
blurb: The TurboGrafx-16, known as the PC Engine outside North America, is a home video game console developed by Hudson Soft and manufactured by NEC. It was released in Japan in 1987 and in North America in 1989.

title: Typewriter
blurb: A machine that stamps letters onto paper through an inked ribbon, one satisfying clack at a time.

title: Ugmonk
blurb: Ugmonk designs analog tools for focused, intentional work, including its Analog card system, and is based in Pennsylvania.

title: Walkman
blurb: Sony's 1979 portable cassette player, which made music something you carry and listen to alone.

title: Widelux
blurb: The Widelux is a fully mechanical swing-lens panoramic camera developed in Japan in 1958 by Panon Camera Shoko. There are both 35mm and medium-format models. Instead of a shutter, the camera has a slit that exposes the film as the lens pivots on a horizontal arc.

title: Wii
about: Home video game console by Nintendo
blurb: The Wii is a home video game console developed and marketed by Nintendo. It was released on November 19, 2006, in North America, and in December 2006 for most other regions of the world.

title: Wii U
about: Home video game console by Nintendo
blurb: The Wii U is a home video game console developed by Nintendo as the successor to the Wii. Released in late 2012, it was the first eighth-generation video game console and competed with Microsoft's Xbox One and Sony's PlayStation 4.

title: Xbox
blurb: The Xbox is a home video game console developed and marketed by Microsoft. It was released on November 15, 2001, in North America, followed by Australia, Europe, and Japan in 2002.

title: Xbox One
blurb: The Xbox One is a home video game console developed by Microsoft. Announced in May 2013, it is the successor to Xbox 360 and the third console in the Xbox series.

title: Xbox Series X and Series S
blurb: The Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S are the fourth generation of consoles in Microsoft's Xbox series, succeeding the previous generation's Xbox One.
